extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for grants (particularly cancer researchers and early-career investigators)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing competitive grant proposals, with emphasis on hypothesis-driven science, preliminary data, feasibility, clarity of writing, mentorship, and responsiveness to reviewers. Targeted toward investigators seeking cancer research funding but broadly applicable to grant applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science must be hypothesis-driven and rigorous
rubrics_metrics.description: A good scientific proposal or research idea should be hypothesis-driven and based on preliminary findings from data with statistical rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid presenting a hypothesis based on questionable data or that jumps to an illogical conclusion. Reviewers will identify scientific holes; flawed science and lack of hypothesis-driven design will lose reviewer enthusiasm. Ensure scope is appropriate and demonstrates potential for direct and meaningful impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data quality and appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Include preliminary findings that meaningfully support your hypothesis and demonstrate statistical rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh what preliminary data to include, why it matters, and how to explain it. Beware small or sparse samples that cannot support the hypothesis, and avoid overly descriptive or convoluted data presentations. Consider how the data will read to a reviewer unfamiliar with your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate scope and demonstrable impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope should not be too large and must demonstrate potential for direct and meaningful impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Too-large scope or failure to show meaningful impact makes grants vulnerable to low scores. Convince reviewers that the proposed research addresses an unmet need and has novel, discernible, and meaningful impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency and alternative plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contingency plans and alternative approaches if the initial hypothesis fails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don’t confuse a viable hypothesis with a fishing expedition. Study goals and approach should be specific, clear, and well-defined, and include what you will do if initial plans 'fall flat.' Lacking backup plans increases risk of being declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem selection: importance, timeliness, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue problems that are timely, critical, pressing, relevant, pragmatic, and address unmet needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not every question is worth funding. Be honest about whether your problem is important relative to other submissions and clearly explain why the research matters now. Avoid pitching research that solves non-existent or irrelevant problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic, achievable aims (avoid over-ambition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set realistic goals and objectives that can achieve measurable outcomes; avoid grandiose promises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overly ambitious or broad promises (e.g., 'we are going to eradicate cancer') raise red flags. Science is incremental; define clear, well-defined, and achievable endpoints to avoid lack of credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, concise, and readable writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Write concisely, clearly, and carefully so reviewers can easily understand your ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid misused words, unnecessary jargon, and long-winded phrasing (use 10 words not 50). Simple, direct prose helps busy reviewers. Have others review for clarity and readability before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and graphics must be easy to understand
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and graphics should clearly demonstrate the goals and desired outcomes of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visuals should be straightforward and support the narrative; complex or unclear figures reduce comprehension and reviewer engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and clear description of funding need
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify the budget and describe the need for funding support in detail so reviewers understand what the project entails and why funds are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear budget justification helps reviewers evaluate feasibility and resource allocation; vague or unjustified budgets undermine confidence in project planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong mentoring plan for career-development grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a solid mentoring plan that indicates career development path and how the current study differs from the mentor’s research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially critical for early-career investigator grants. Explain mentorship structure, training goals, and how mentorship will support independence. Demonstrate learning and career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting documents: letters, biosketch, and personal statement consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Include sufficient supporting documents and recommendation letters that demonstrate feasibility and applicant credibility; ensure consistency across letters, biosketch, and personal statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters of support should corroborate institutional backing and feasibility; materials must align with application guidelines and deadlines. Inconsistencies reduce credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional support and reliable safety net
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate strong institutional support and that a reliable team/mentoring network exists to navigate challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funders invest in people and institutions; show the expertise and experience available to the investigator and how institutional resources will enable project success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address reviewer feedback when resubmitting
rubrics_metrics.description: When resubmitting after rejection, graciously and thoroughly address all review committee feedback from the prior attempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond point-by-point to concerns raised, show changes or provide rebuttals where justified. Demonstrating responsiveness increases chances on resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek external critical review before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject your application to constructive criticism from people who know more and whose judgment you trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicit feedback for clarity, readability, and scientific rigor. Recognize fallibility and use feedback to strengthen hypotheses, data presentation, and writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid typographical and basic errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate typographical errors and basic mistakes that make the application appear careless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple errors can undermine reviewer confidence; proofread carefully and have others check for typos and formatting issues.
